what: The store's reader gives a value whole or not at all: `get` checks and pins every page of the record, `pinned` holds them all for as long as the caller keeps the value. A def map record read for one name therefore loaded the crate's whole record, and a dependency image is pinned whole for a session. To read one name's pages I had to add `Reader::part` in the store lane's files.
cost: an hour reading read.rs to find what a ranged read may trust; one additive method in another lane's file
cause: every reader so far wanted the whole value (a template, a unit record), so the pool's ranged pin (`Look::pack_bytes`) was never given a public door
whys: why whole: a value is verified by its one content hash
why is that enough for a part: the pool checks every block against its file's checks as it loads it, so after one whole verification a part is of bytes that were hashed
why was it not exposed: no record was large and read sparsely until def maps were
why does a session pin an image whole: `Held` is one buffer of bytes, with no notion of a read's lifetime
class: an interface that offers only the whole of a thing whose readers want a part
prevention: `hir_def::deps::PageSource` is the one way a front-end record is read: a part, held for the read; the image's `Held` (whole, for the session) is to go as each part of the image becomes a record of its own (restore.md, 'Def maps read in place', what it does not do yet (1))
state: open: lang items and signatures are still read from the pinned image
